Sony’s PlayStation Disc Decision Is Its Biggest Scandal in 20 Years

Forbes · July 2, 2026 · Opinion

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original article

Analysis

This article, written by Paul Tassi, is written to tell the reader of past mistakes made by PlayStation and compare them to the end of production of discs, calling it their “Biggest Scandal in 20 Years.”

Tassi claims that one reason this is PlayStation’s worst decision is how outraged people are about it. He mentions how many replies there were on the original announcement, most of which were not positive about the change. Despite him saying it is such a big mistake, he does not believe that PlayStation will go back on this choice. In his writing, he calls PlayStation an “immovable object” to show how much he thinks they are set in their decision.

This article is very much an opinionated article to express the opinion of the writer. The article starts off by introducing the subject briefly before jumping into talking about past mistakes by Sony to express just how big this is compared to other controversies in the past. It uses a lot of pathos to play on the emotions of the readers while not citing credible sources or stats that are relevant to the disc issue other than his stats on the post. We are unable to verify exactly whether 99% of comments were furious. All in all, it can be used as a reliable source but should be used cautiously due to the lack of sources and the unverifiable percentage of outrage.

Digital Gamer, Wants Ownership and Competition

Reddit · July 17, 2026 · Player perspective

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original post

Analysis

The point of this post is to raise the question of whether this decision of PlayStation’s is a good idea or not.

The writer brings up that they are a long-time fan of PlayStation and even at one point collected physical PlayStation media, but at this point they mostly use a digital library. Despite this, they are still sad about the change and can see how it could ruin stores that rely on this physical media. The author believes this is how the rest of the console industry will shift eventually. The author brings up the point of lack of true ownership and expresses their opinion that digital ownership is weak right now.

The author tries to use ethos by first introducing themselves and how they are related to the topic. Additionally, they use pathos by calling this the “end of an era.” Nonetheless, the post is mostly based on opinion, and its theories about other consoles, although possible, cannot be verified. Despite this, this source is great for showing their side of the argument even though, as they stated, the change will have little direct effect on them.

Joni Lappalainen on the shift to digital

LinkedIn · Joni Lappalainen

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original post

Analysis

The purpose is to inform the reader of why the writer, Joni Lappalainen, believes this to be the next step in technology.

Lappalainen starts off by calling discs a “thing of the past.” He reasons that at this point most people do not care about physical movies or TV and that games would go the same way eventually. He acknowledges people like collectors and mentions how studios will still probably make something like a case with an activation code for the game inside. He brings up the fact that by stopping the production of discs, the upcoming PlayStation 6 could be designed without a disc reader, possibly reducing costs. Finally, Lappalainen discusses the fact that he believes that in the world today, we already don’t really own anything that can’t be taken away by stuff like the government or inflation.

In this article, Lappalainen uses logos when addressing how things went with physical movies and TV. His claims about people’s opinions of physical media and about studios making physical collectibles, though, are unproven by him. Taking this into account, this article can be used to see his side of the argument, but some facts should be checked first.

PlayStation will stop releasing games on discs in 2028

BBC News · 2026

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original article

Analysis

The purpose of this article is to inform the reader of the change and what it may affect while also including quotes from other people that may contain opinions of their own.

BBC mentions how this new change is a big milestone in the industry’s switch away from physical discs as sales of physical media have lessened over time. The article also shows how many people disagree about whether this is a good decision or a bad one, showing examples of quotes from people who believe this change to be what pushes us to the next advance and people who are concerned about how no longer having physical media will affect ownership, profit from physical stores, and even the transfer of ownership of digital games.

In this article, BBC uses a lot of ethos by quoting many people familiar with such subjects. This use of ethos, while showing parts of both sides, is unable to show everything since there are more quotes for the side against the change. With this information, this article can be trusted as informative on the sides of the argument, but not completely due to the fact it includes more opinions from the side against the change than for, but this does not mean it is false.

The End of Ownership

Slate · July 7, 2026

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original article

Analysis

The purpose of this article is to have the reader draw the conclusion that PlayStation has not made a good decision to stop the production of physical discs.

Pahwa brings up that despite this being what PlayStation believes to be the next step due to the decrease in physical media sales, many consumers think not. He talks about how many people have commented negatively on the change and people have even gone as far as to make a petition with nearly 180,000 signatures at that time and almost 390,000 when checked on 11/10/2026. He then goes to mention how, despite the lower sales of physical media, PlayStation still sold 70 million discs in 2025, which is no small amount. He goes on to cover both the topics of ownership rights and people’s collections of discs they will be unable to continue growing.

Throughout this article, there is a very strong bias against PlayStation and their decision. He uses logos by showing the stats: nearly 180,000 petition signatures against the change and 70 million discs sold in 2025. He also uses lots of exaggerated language such as “absolutely boiling” and “earth-shattering quake.” Because of all of this, the article can be used for some information but should mostly be analyzed as biased and used to show the side against this change.

Physical disc production ending in January 2028 for new games

PlayStation · July 1, 2026 · Official statement

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original article

Analysis

The purpose is to inform the reader of the new change and how the end of physical media would work.

PlayStation claims that this change in the end of production of physical game discs for PlayStation consoles is due to the lower sales of physical media. They call it the natural direction for the company to move to continue with modernity.

This source is completely biased toward the change because it is the announcement article. It can be taken as the primary source on what PlayStation plans on doing and their reasoning on the change. The article uses ethos simply by being from PlayStation and uses logos by referring to the shift in how media is purchased, which caused them to make this change. This source should be used as a primary source of information.

Sony to drop support for physical media confirming post-disc gaming world

Ampere Analysis · Piers Harding-Rolls · July 1, 2026

Open the original source (online) ↗

Original article

Analysis

The purpose of Ampere Analysis’s article, written by Piers Harding-Rolls, is to inform readers about PlayStation stopping production of discs and give insight into how this may affect the future.

This article presents how, though consoles are “the last hold-out for physical media in the gaming sector”, it has been declining over the years from 87% physical in 2013 to a little over 20% in 2025.

Piers continues to go on to talk about how publishers will have much less to worry about financially, because with discs, the publisher would have to put a lot into overhead before publishing, but with no physical media, there would be no need for them to pay for this. Despite this, he also entertains the possibility of new costs that may be added by PlayStation.

All in all, this article is written to be an informational article to educate the reader on PlayStation’s announcement to stop physical game disc production. It lays out many facts such as game creator fees and the decline in the retail industry. It allows the reader to draw their own conclusions by presenting all of this in an informational way, but it does use exaggerated language a couple of times such as inevitable and certainly guarantees. Because of all of this, it is informational and a good source for anyone interested in the controversy behind the ending of production for physical PlayStation discs.

PlayStation and Physical Games

PlayStation sets the end of physical game production for 2028 raising much concern and contention from the community.

Explore the topic

Background

In July 2026, PlayStation announced that they would slowly stop all production of physical game discs by 2028. After this post, there was much uproar in the community over what this may mean from physical businesses no longer having products to sell to concerns about what ownership means when you have no power over something.

Sony says this change does not affect games released on disc before January 2028. The announcement does not say that existing discs will suddenly stop working.

78%

of PS4 and PS5 full-game units sold in the fiscal year ending March 2026 were downloads.

Digital downloads: 78%Other formats: 22%

The debate

PlayStation’s reasoning for this change is valid. With the dramatically shrinking market for these physical discs, there seems to be less reason for the infrastructure and complications when an online marketplace is so much easier. Additionally, they have stated that after buying a game at a retailer, instead of a disc, you will receive a code for the game to help these industries despite the change.

Concerns about losing discs

Many people have expressed concern about losing physical discs for many reasons, but one of these is collection. Many people have collected game discs, and by removing the production of them, collections like this would no longer be possible. Other concerns include sharing of games, offline play, and long-term access.

QuestionPhysical discDigital download
SharingWith a physical disc, friends and family are easily able to let others borrow their media, and if they need a quick buck, they can sell these discs to others.Sharing with a digital download has raised many concerns about whether it will be possible and, if so, how it will work. Currently, if you purchase a game digitally, you cannot sell it to others, nor can you share it with your friends.
Offline playWith a physical disc, you can simply place it in the console and play without an internet connection.To play a digital game, you must first download the game from the store, which requires an internet connection.
Long-term accessWith a physical game, as long as the disc is intact, you will be able to play that game whenever you want.With a digital download, as soon as the game is removed from PlayStation’s official backend archive, you will be unable to download it again.

In 2023, a study found that 87% of games released in the U.S. before 2010 were no longer available.
Source: Video Game History Foundation’s 2023 game availability study.

My perspective

The change PlayStation will make in ending the production of new physical game discs is misguided. By doing so, they have raised many concerns involving ownership rights, feasibility of collecting, sharing, and offline use, and many more possible issues with physical media and the end thereof.

The Reddit user from the source above stated, “I absolutely want TRUE OWNERSHIP and COMPETITION.” They, being someone that mostly purchases digital games, are concerned about what this shift to all digital could mean for ownership rights. This shows that even people who mostly use digital copies still see the value in keeping physical versions. One good thing to keep in mind though is what Harding-Rolls mentioned concerning the “financial risk” that would now be lessened for publishers but also how additional costs may be added by PlayStation.

Although there seem to be some upsides to this change, such as possibly lower costs for publishers, there are still many concerns that will simply not be able to be resolved without physical game discs and other issues, such as possible fees to publishers that we just cannot predict. For example, collectors will just not get the same satisfaction from buying a digital copy of a game. In addition, those people wanting to share games, sell their games, or play completely offline will have these options severely limited compared to beforehand. Because of these reasons, to preserve the satisfaction of consumers, I believe that this change by PlayStation should be reconsidered and removed.
